skills.name: The Great Depression: manifestations, responses and consequences

note.text: The Depression brought severe unemployment, falling output and prices, business failures and hardship. Trade contraction affected exporters, including colonial economies dependent on a narrow range of products. Governments responded differently through relief, public works, financial reform or other policies. Roosevelt’s New Deal began in 1933 in the United States. Political extremism gained opportunities in some settings, but dictatorship was not an inevitable or identical outcome everywhere. Recovery timing varied, and the American chronology should not be imposed on every country.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain economic hardship and varied political responses without treating dictatorship as inevitable. Builds on: boom vulnerabilities, crash and banking contraction. Leads to: regional cooperation and international economic relationships.

sections.heading: Explain the history

Trade contraction affected exporters, including colonial economies dependent on a narrow range of products. Political extremism gained opportunities in some settings, but dictatorship was not an inevitable or identical outcome everywhere. sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: A fall in export earnings could reduce colonial producers’ incomes even without a local stock exchange. Falling prices could coexist with lower incomes and debt difficulties. Relief and reform were responses, not proof that every policy solved every problem immediately. Compare causes with manifestations and longer-term consequences using a specific country and period.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and period before explaining a relationship. Use the practice text only for the claim it supports. Distinguish a cause, an event and an outcome; compare authentic sources before treating an interpretation as established. A sequence alone does not prove that every later outcome was inevitable.

key_words.meaning: an observable feature of the downturn such as unemployment or falling output
exposure of an export-dependent economy to falling overseas demand or prices
action intended to address hardship or financial instability
political changes whose outcome depended on the particular setting

cards.idea: Connect a specific action or event to the historical feature it illustrates.
example: Factories reduced production and many workers lost jobs.
Lower world demand reduced earnings from a narrow export base.
The New Deal introduced US relief and reform measures from {1933}.
Extremist movements gained opportunities in some affected countries.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: A depression is defined by every household enjoying rising employment. Correction: The stated manifestations show contraction and hardship.
A country needed its own major share market to be affected. Correction: Trade could transmit hardship through export earnings.
A policy announcement proves an immediate universal recovery. Correction: Results require evidence and differed across measures and time.
Every affected country inevitably became the same kind of dictatorship. Correction: Economic crisis interacted with institutions and political choices.
